Adding an AI chat to a website is easy. Running it responsibly is where the design matters. The difficult parts are not only model quality, but deciding what the AI may answer, where it should send visitors, which URLs may be displayed, and how API cost is controlled.

Acecore added an AI contact chat to a static Astro + Cloudflare Pages site. The main implementation is in [the PR that added the contact AI and CMS-scoped translation flow]({ACECORE_KEEP_270acb4d7b12_URL_25}). ## Overall Structure

The architecture has {ACECORE_KEEP_270acb4d7b12_NUMBER_3_27} simple layers.

| Layer                | Responsibility                                                          |
| -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Chat widget          | UI, input, current locale, minimal history, and Markdown rendering      |
| {ACECORE_KEEP_270acb4d7b12_CODE_28}    | Validation, Origin checks, rate limiting, prompt construction, AI calls |
| OpenAI Responses API | Generate an answer from public site context and conversation state      |

Keeping the model call behind a server-side endpoint prevents key exposure, lets you update the model, prompts and site context server-side, and centralizes input length limits, Origin checks, rate limits and error handling in {ACECORE_KEEP_270acb4d7b12_NUMBER_1_38} place.

## Keep the Endpoint Contract Small

The request payload should stay narrow.

{ACECORE_KEEP_270acb4d7b12_CODE_32}

Names, email addresses, phone numbers, company names, and detailed form fields do not need to go through the AI chat. The chat is an entry point for helping users decide which service to read about and which contact route to use.

History should also be limited. Send only recent turns and enforce a character limit per {ACECORE_KEEP_270acb4d7b12_NUMBER_1_49} message. This keeps prompts smaller and controls API cost.

The important point is to reduce and validate input before calling the AI API. The AI API incurs costs for the input it receives. Long messages, unnecessary history, and repeated access from external sites can make operations unstable before the feature itself becomes useful.

For a site of this size, you do not need to start with a vector database or RAG. A structured prompt context made from public site information is easier to operate.

Useful context includes:

- Company and service summaries
- Target users, example consultations, and related URLs for each service
- FAQ content that already answers common questions
- Rules for forms, LINE, email, and phone
- Areas the AI must not assert, such as pricing, contracts, or schedules
- Internal URLs for each locale

The goal is not to let the model answer from what it generally knows. The goal is to tell it what this site is allowed to say.

This approach is sufficient while the site has few pages. As page count, update frequency, and search requirements grow, consider adding a search layer using Pagefind, CMS JSON, D{ACECORE_KEEP_270acb4d7b12_NUMBER_1_30}, Vectorize, or similar tools.

The prompt should define answer boundaries and restrictions more than writing style.

{ACECORE_KEEP_270acb4d7b12_CODE_39}

A common failure is for the model to make firm promises while trying to make a service look good. For questions such as “How much will it cost?”, “When can you deliver?” and “Can you guarantee support?”, provide general guidance and send the visitor to the form for a formal answer.

This is not only a legal issue: estimates and delivery dates cannot be fixed before hearing the requirements. Write the range of answers the operation can stand behind into the prompt, rather than merely answers that are convenient for sales.

The AI chat should not replace the contact form. The contact page works better when each route has a clear role.

| Route          | Role                                                               |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| FAQ            | Resolve common questions on the page                               |
| AI chat        | Help visitors choose services, contact routes, and related pages   |
| LINE           | Quick questions, Acecore Schools inquiries, and lightweight checks |
| Form           | Estimates, production inquiries, partnerships, and recruiting      |
| Direct contact | Follow-up after the form or urgent confirmation only               |

The AI connects broad service content such as the [service overview article](/services/) with concrete routes on the [contact page](/contact/). This pattern works for BtoB sites, agencies, schools, and SaaS support pages. It is easier to introduce when the goal is to narrow down the next page or contact method, rather than complete the inquiry through AI.

- Paragraphs
- Lists
- Bold text
- Inline code

A small, strict renderer is easier to reason about than a full Markdown implementation. If you allow more external links, at least use a domain allowlist and {ACECORE_KEEP_270acb4d7b12_CODE_57}.

Astro dev or preview is not identical to the Cloudflare Pages Functions environment. Without {ACECORE_KEEP_270acb4d7b12_CODE_58}, local testing should focus on UI fallback and error states.

## Watch the Right Operational Signals

After release, watch more than page views.

- API error rate
- Rate-limit hits
- Average messages per {ACECORE_KEEP_270acb4d7b12_NUMBER_1_63} inquiry
- Clicks to the form and LINE
- Cases where the AI could not answer and guided users to the form
- Usage by locale

If you store conversation text, define the privacy rules first. A safer first step is to store event counts and errors without message bodies.

## What Is Left for Another Article

This article focuses only on the technical design of the AI contact chat. Passing service-page context into the contact form is also implemented, and that is covered in [Technical design for passing context from a service CTA to the contact form](/blog/service-cta-contact-prefill/).

- AI chat: organize uncertainty through conversation and guide users safely
- Service CTA: pass the service context a visitor is reading into the form

The former concerns AI, API boundaries, prompts, and safe rendering; the latter concerns form UX and navigation design. Keeping them separate makes both articles easier to read and easier to cross-link later.

## Summary

When adding an AI contact chat to a static site, design the API boundary and answer controls before polishing the UI.

The key decisions were:

- Call OpenAI from a Cloudflare Pages Function, not the browser
- Keep endpoint input small and limit history and message length
- Build site context and locale-aware URLs on the server side
- Put clear boundaries in the prompt for what the AI may not assert
- Split the roles of forms, LINE, and direct contact
- Add Origin checks and rate limiting
- Render Markdown links through a trimmed allowlist

Static sites can support useful AI contact chats. The point is not to make the AI visible, but to help visitors choose their next action safely.

## Итоги

При добавлении AI-чата для обращений к статическому сайту важнее сначала спроектировать границу API и управление ответами, чем интерфейс чата.

В этой реализации особенно полезны следующие решения:

- вызывать OpenAI API из Cloudflare Pages Function, а не из браузера;
- минимизировать вход endpoint и ограничить историю и длину сообщений;
- формировать информацию сайта и URL для каждого языка на сервере;
- указывать в промпте, какие утверждения AI может и не может делать;
- разделить роли формы, LINE и прямых контактов;
- проверять Origin и ограничивать частоту запросов;
- удалять пробелы вокруг URL и выводить Markdown-ссылки по списку разрешённых адресов.

AI-чат для обращений вполне можно реализовать на статическом сайте. Главное при внедрении — помочь посетителю безопасно выбрать следующее действие.
